title.narrative: Provision of Life-Saving Food Assistance and Livelihood Protection to Vulnerable Pastoral Households in Bosaso District, Northern Somalia, through Unconditional Cash and Livestock Inputs

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to improve household food security and protect livelihoods for 1300 drought-affected and food-insecure households (1,200 vulnerable households, 7,200 individuals — 1,944 women, 1,908 girls, 1,656 men, and 1,692 boys) in 10 villages of northern Somalia: Ufeyn, Kobdhaxaad, Carmo, Carta, Ceeldaahir, Barookhle, Iaaso Dawaco, Laag, Conqor, and Balidoog. The project will prioritize the most vulnerable households, including 15% persons with disabilities and marginalized groups, who face heightened risks due to the prolonged drought and loss of productive assets. Following successive below-average rainfall seasons and poor livestock conditions, most households in northern Somalia are experiencing IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) or Phase 4 (Emergency) food insecurity. To address this, KAALO proposes to provide unconditional cash transfers of USD 65 per household per month for four months. This assistance is designed to cover approximately 70% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), enabling targeted households to access essential food and basic needs through local markets. In addition to cash transfers, the project will support 370 vulnerable pastoral households with emergency livestock inputs such as supplementary feed and water trucking, aimed at protecting core breeding animals and restoring minimal productive capacity. These combined interventions are expected to stabilize household food consumption, reduce negative coping mechanisms, and prevent further livelihood erosion in drought-affected communities. Implementation will be carried out directly by KAALO through an inclusive community-based targeting (ICBT) process, ensuring transparent selection in coordination with village committees and local authorities. Beneficiary registration, mobile money transfer arrangements, and regular disbursements will follow standardized SHF accountability and monitoring procedures. A post-distribution monitoring (PDM) exercise will be conducted to assess beneficiary satisfaction, efficiency of delivery mechanisms, and the project’s impact on food security outcomes. KAALO will coordinate closely with humanitarian partners and local authorities in Puntland to prevent overlap, ensure complementarity with ongoing responses, and enhance resilience among drought-affected pastoral populations. By restoring immediate access to food and protecting critical livestock assets, this project aims to mitigate the worsening food insecurity and enhance the recovery capacity of highly vulnerable households in northern Somalia.lt/pgt
